protocol: D-000; independent adversarial review; refute not confirm; DR-105/DR-114 actor scope
summary: Option B is the right answer and its central justification checks out at bytes: permission-truth-tables.v1's deliberateNonTokens list has exactly four members, and the fourth is 'host-initiated writes to a user-named output path … NOT a component permission, and not in the truth table' — precisely the host-under-user-instruction case, so clause 1's 'fourth deliberate non-token' citation is exact rather than rhetorical. The entry also breaks BLK-5, the circular deferral the whole join turns on, by ruling that doctor consent is never a DR-105 grant. It does not smuggle a design: clause 4 declines to mint a host-effect truth table and clause 6 applies neither candidate. Two MUST-FIX defects stand. First, the claim that join consequences are 'stated not waved' does not survive measurement — three of the seven blockers get no statement at all, and a fourth survives in exactly the case clause 3 keeps inside DR-105. Second, the entry omits the reversibility class and the readiness effect, both of which D-000 clause 3 requires and this review prompt names.

objections.claim: The entry states its join consequences as 'stated not waved', but four of the seven blockers are not disposed: BLK-2, BLK-6 and BLK-7 receive no statement anywhere in the entry, and BLK-4 survives the disposition in the component-tail case clause 3 expressly keeps inside DR-105.
objections.evidence: Measured from the join verdict at 538f368156d22f96bf067dd9faad924610dd78ca16968ad46541efcf14a61344, whose $.blockers is a seven-element list. Mapping the entry's six consequence bullets against it: BLK-1 (CA-2 needs the execute-anything grant DR-105 withheld) is disposed by bullet 6; BLK-3 (doctor's closed status set cannot carry INDETERMINATE or COMPLETED-BEFORE-REVOCATION) by bullet 3; BLK-5 (the circular deferral, DR-105 deferring 'is a doctor consent a journal grant?' to DR-114 and doctor deferring back) by clause 2's 'never a DR-105 grant' — the cleanest work in the entry. The remaining four are not. BLK-2 records that CA-3 probes span four effects of which none has a token — keychain RESERVED under deferred DR-108, local socket / named pipe RESERVED, out-of-root — and the entry never mentions CA-3, probes' effect set, keychain, sockets or out-of-root access. BLK-6 records that four DR-105 tokens, FS-READ-PROJECT, FS-READ-COMPONENT, FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE and ENV-READ, describe effects doctor performs in its UNCONSENTED default posture; the entry names none of them and never addresses the unconsented default. BLK-7 is a measurement defect — doctor's /whatThisDoesNotDo/2 asserts 'no DR-105 artifact exists in the measured tree', which the reviewer measured as false at current bytes — and the entry is silent. BLK-4 records that DR-105's journal-every-acceptance rule collides mechanically with doctor's FC-RO byte-immutability fixture; clause 2's 'never journaled' answers this for host consent, but clause 3 keeps component tails in DR-105 with 'DR-105 tokens / REQUESTED-from-manifest / grant journal', so when doctor spawns an admitted component the journal-every-acceptance rule applies and the collision with doctor's read-only fixture returns unaddressed. Bullet 1's 'Totality of CA-1..CA-4 over DR-105 tokens is inapplicable' cannot carry the missing four: it dissolves the totality for host acts, which is exactly the set clause 3 removes from the tail, and BLK-2, BLK-4 and BLK-6 all bite on effects that are either component-executed or performed by doctor itself without consent.
objections.proposedFix: Extend clause 5 to state a consequence for BLK-2, BLK-4, BLK-6 and BLK-7 by name. For BLK-2 and BLK-6 the Option B logic plausibly dissolves them — host-executed probes and doctor's own unconsented reads fall outside DR-105 — but that has to be said, and the component-executed probe case has to be resolved rather than assumed. For BLK-4 state how the journal-every-acceptance rule and doctor's FC-RO fixture coexist on the component tail. BLK-7 is a factual defect in the doctor candidate rather than an actor-scope question; if it is out of scope, route it by name to DR-114 rather than leaving it unmentioned.

objections.claim: The entry omits the reversibility class and the readiness effect, both required by D-000 clause 3 and both named by this review prompt.
objections.evidence: Measured: the draft contains zero occurrences of 'Readiness effect', 'Reversibility' or 're-measured'. Its only closing section is '## Overturn — Supersession + revert of C-D032', which supplies the overturn procedure but no class. D-000's entry format requires 'id, date, title, status, decision, alternatives considered, rationale, reviewer + verdict + digest, decision type, REVERSIBILITY, overturn procedure, commit'. Checked against that list D-032 supplies id, date, title, status, decision, alternatives, rationale via its Honesty section, and decision type (PREFERENCE-LADEN, correctly marked); reversibility class and readiness effect are the gaps. Neither is merely formal here. The overturn clause is also flat where this lineage has established that it should not be: the adopted D-028, D-029 and D-030 each carry a temporal boundary distinguishing total reversibility before a dependent lands from the compound overturn required afterwards, and D-032 has obvious dependents — clause 6 states that 'Successors must conform to this disposition or contest it', so a permission-truth-tables or doctor-contract successor written against this disposition is exactly such a dependent. And the readiness effect is substantive rather than nil-by-inspection: the entry dispositions the join blocking two OPEN register rows, DR-105 and DR-114, both of which I verified remain OPEN at file 08's current bytes.
objections.proposedFix: Add a readiness-effect statement — most likely zero row-status movement, since clause 6 applies neither candidate, but it must be stated rather than inferred — and a reversibility class with the temporal boundary the adopted siblings use: total before a conforming successor lands, compound afterwards, naming the successor class that must be superseded or reverted alongside it.

objections.claim: Two of the six consequences are unresolved disjunctions rather than dispositions, so the entry's own framing of them as 'stated' overstates what they settle.
objections.evidence: Bullet 2 reads 'permissionRef stays permanently reserved or is withdrawn.' Those are different outcomes with different consequences for the doctor candidate — a permanently reserved binding point leaves a field in the schema that nothing may ever fill, while withdrawal removes it — and the entry picks neither. The join verdict's own $.verdictBasis.whatThisVerdictIsNOT records that 'doctor keeps consentRecord.permissionRef a RESERVED BINDING POINT', so this is the live question the join surfaced and the entry leaves it open. Bullet 5 reads 'PT-NET-EGRESS's slice-1 posture, if host-executed doctor egress, re-binds to DR-114's consent record; if component-executed, it stays DR-105.' That is a correct statement of the rule but not a disposition, because which branch obtains in slice 1 is a fact about D-002's doctor, and the entry does not decide or cite it. A successor author reading clause 6's instruction to 'conform to this disposition' cannot conform to a disjunction.
objections.proposedFix: Choose permanently-reserved or withdrawn for permissionRef, or route the choice by name to DR-114 with an owner. For PT-NET-EGRESS, state which branch slice-1 doctor egress takes, or record explicitly that the branch is undecided and name where it is decided.

objections.claim: The entry cites doctor-contract.v2 as the live candidate twice, which is stale after D-035, and it carries no digest for either candidate artifact and no re-measurement clause to catch the drift.
objections.evidence: The draft contains exactly one hex digest — the join verdict at 538f368156d22f96bf067dd9faad924610dd78ca16968ad46541efcf14a61344, which I re-measured and confirms correct — and zero occurrences of 're-measured' or an equivalent clause. Its two other substantive citations are unpinned: the Question section routes by 'doctor-contract.v2 identityDependencies ID-DEP-12', and clause 6 states 'This entry does not apply permission-truth-tables.v1 or doctor-contract.v2. Both remain candidates.' Measured against the register at 9d41c5ba, file 08's DR-114 row now reads 'OPEN — design contract ACCEPTED 2026-08-13 (D-035); the actor-join and fixture-execution halves remain open', naming doctor-contract.v4.json, which exists at df2e717555616db096e61548458f23b442f7f0e37b2d2461eabc2c33201e94b3 with documentClass DESIGN-CONTRACT-CANDIDATE. So v2 is not the live candidate and clause 6's 'Both remain candidates' misstates v2's standing. I record two mitigations honestly. The routing content survives: ID-DEP-12 is present in v2, v3 and v4 alike, so the entry points at something real. And the draft's own header says 'Not yet dispatched', so v4's acceptance post-dates authoring — I therefore do not score this as a wrong digest. What I score is that dispatching for adoption review without re-measurement, in a draft with no re-measurement clause, is how the staleness reaches a reviewer at all; every other draft in this lineage carried that clause for exactly this case.
objections.proposedFix: Re-point both citations to doctor-contract.v4 at df2e7175…, pin permission-truth-tables.v1 at 0f73f31c…, correct clause 6's characterization of v2's standing, and add the re-measurement clause the sibling drafts carry.

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 574a07a4c5f316b6ed4689bb93eb42ad9d959e092bf047cbf29b08f008f99226 both times. No drift.

The 'fourth deliberate non-token' citation, which is clause 1's whole warrant, is exact. permission-truth-tables.v1 at 0f73f31cffccc85d10c71596f05ed1e00d044cff12b9ecf56a1aa8c44f973632 carries $.permissionVocabulary.deliberateNonTokens as a four-element list: clock/wall-clock, entropy/randomness, host output, and fourth 'host-initiated writes to a user-named output path (e.g. analyze --output report.sarif) — NOT a component permission, and not in the truth table.' That fourth member is the host-under-user-instruction case, so Option B restates DR-105's own ruling rather than reversing it, and the count 'fourth' is right.

The join verdict re-measured at 538f368156d22f96bf067dd9faad924610dd78ca16968ad46541efcf14a61344, matching the draft's pin. $.verdict is INCOHERENT and $.blockers is a seven-element list with ids BLK-1 through BLK-7, each carrying refs and a oneLine. I read all seven and mapped them against the entry's six consequence bullets; that mapping is the basis of C2-D032-01.

Does it smuggle a design into doctor or DR-105: NO, and this is the axis I expected to find something on. Clause 4 states 'No new permission vocabulary is minted here' and defers a host-effect truth table to 'a later isolated entry … if product wants one'. Clause 6 applies neither candidate and leaves both as candidates. Clause 2's properties of the consent record — named at invocation or by pre-existing policy, invocation-bound, in memory, in the post-report, never journaled — read as constraints on any successor rather than as a schema, and they are all negative or scoping rather than structural. The one term that could be new, 'doctor-side record', is descriptive; doctor's own existing term consentRecord is what the join verdict quotes.

Option A and Option C get a fair hearing. A is rejected on three independent grounds — it reverses DR-105's deliberate non-token, it requires grant-binding identities doctor does not mint (ID-DEP-10), and it models the user as authorizing against themselves — the first of which I verified at bytes above. C is rejected as the default rather than as wrong, on cost, on still needing a host regime, and on the observation that the entry already keeps the one split that is real, with an explicit invitation for a successor to refine the tail boundary. Neither rejection is a strawman.

The component-tail rule is genuinely a split rather than a blanket exemption: clause 3 keeps spawned admitted components (the CA-1 child-process half) and component-originated egress (the CA-4 component half) inside DR-105 with tokens, REQUESTED-from-manifest and the grant journal, and draws the line at 'the host's decision to spawn is doctor consent; the child's subsequent effects are DR-105.' That is the correct place for the line and it is what makes BLK-4's survival a real finding rather than a quibble.
Decision type is present and correct: PREFERENCE-LADEN, in the header block. This is the field D-036 omits, so the two drafts fail D-000 clause 3 in different places.

DR-105 and DR-114 are both still OPEN in file 08 at 5e1a75a542c3a4914d44a5093a057d89a39e140b84011a85d56ed0d769c19f07 — DR-105 'OPEN — candidate authored 2026-08-13, independent review DISPATCHED and not yet returned', DR-114 'OPEN — design contract ACCEPTED 2026-08-13 (D-035); the actor-join and fixture-execution halves remain open'. The actor-join half is exactly what this entry addresses, so the entry is aimed at a live gap.
ID-DEP-12, the routing dependency the Question section names, is present in doctor-contract v2, v3 and v4 alike, so the stale version pin does not point at vanished content.
No silent D-001 or D-002 amendment. The entry touches neither the five readiness conditions nor D-002's sets; it dispositions a coherence defect between two OPEN design candidates.
whatIDidNotCheck: The Codex verdict on D-032. Not read; confirmed absent from docs/coop/artifacts at review time.

Whether Option B is the right product answer. It is preference-laden and inside the coordinator's D-000 authority. I checked that its stated warrant is true at bytes, that the alternatives were fairly stated, and that its consequences are complete — the third is where it fails.
The full contents of permission-truth-tables.v1 and doctor-contract.v4 beyond the selectors named here. Both are OPEN candidates and neither is applied by this entry.

Whether the four blockers I found unaddressed would in fact dissolve under Option B. I state that BLK-2 and BLK-6 plausibly do for the host-executed and unconsented-default cases; establishing that is the coordinator's work, not mine, and my finding is that the entry does not attempt it.
BLK-7's underlying measurement — whether doctor's /whatThisDoesNotDo/2 is false at current bytes. I took the join reviewer's measurement as given and scored only the entry's silence about it.
D-033 through D-036 as entries, except D-035's effect on DR-114's status and D-036, which I reviewed separately in this session against its own prompt.

environment.authoringVersusDispatch: The draft's header states 'Not yet dispatched' and 'Not dispatched while Claude 2 / Codex are on D-025–D-031', so it was authored before D-035 accepted doctor-contract.v4. I did not score its v2 citations as wrong-at-authoring; C2-D032-04 scores the absence of a re-measurement clause, which is what let the staleness survive into dispatch.
environment.note: The subject and review prompt are untracked working-tree files at review time; digests bind working-tree bytes, not committed objects. Recorded as a condition of review, not a finding, since the draft is pre-adoption and binds nothing.
environment.measurementTool: shasum -a 256; python3 json for $.blockers, $.permissionVocabulary.deliberateNonTokens and artifact headers; grep -cE for hex-digest detection; awk field extraction for file-08 rows

convergenceNote: The substantive choice survives attack. Option B is warranted at bytes, the alternatives are fairly rejected, no design is smuggled, no vocabulary is minted, and BLK-5 — the circular deferral the join turns on — is genuinely broken. Neither MUST-FIX contests the choice. C2-D032-01 asks the entry to finish the work it claims to have done, covering four blockers it left silent, and two of those four plausibly dissolve under the rule it already states. C2-D032-02 asks for two sections the adopted siblings carry. Both are additive.
